results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 51 outline summaries match the controlling ideas of their aligned spec paragraphs (p01-p51) in spec order; the three opening callouts match no paragraph.

results.draft_locus: A Refund Is a Second Payment, and It Can Fail ¶3
results.quote: A refund also does not undo the cost of the sale.
results.finding: The unit holds two ideas with separate evidence: the merchant's fees are not returned, and ("The customer waits as well") the customer waits days or weeks. The spec's own controlling idea for p15 joins the same two claims with 'and'. The other units marked two_ideas (Introduction ¶5, Outside Cards ¶3, In Practice ¶4) hold one idea with an appendix, two cases of one range, or a consequence.
Every body unit ties to one of S1-S5 as its section declares; introduction and conclusion units frame or synthesize the same claims.

Each table and figure has a lead-in or caption saying what it shows, and each quotation is introduced or followed by its reading (for example 'a message about a promise, not about money', 'Winning recovers money and leaves the ratio where it was').

Every declared transition is readable at its boundary. The weakest are the openings of 'Three Routes Back', 'How a Card Dispute Runs' and 'Two Design Decisions', where the relationship is carried by the heading and an implicit link, not by an explicit pick-up of the declared known information.

results.draft_locus: A Refund Is a Second Payment, and It Can Fail ¶2
results.quote: The table shows the same gap on all three routes; the next section explains its dispute row.
results.finding: Both readers could not read the table's dispute row where it stands: its last cell ("Yes, in both directions") points to things explained only in the provider comparison and the failure section, and the next section does not explain it as promised. The first two cells are readable from the dispute's definition, so the row's wording and the unkept pointer are the draft's.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, item 3 (first reported by flow reader 1, item 6)

results.draft_locus: How a Card Dispute Runs: The Issuer Decides, on the Issuer's Clock ¶4
results.quote: lists Mastercard's stages as notification of chargeback, chargeback, information supplied, chargeback reversed, pre-arbitration, second chargeback and scheme arbitration
results.finding: Both readers call this the hardest paragraph: seven stage names arrive unexplained, and 'chargeback reversed' and 'second chargeback', on which the provider comparison and the worked example depend, are explained only later.

results.finding: The introduction opens on a dated scenario and a question, states the thesis and gives a roadmap; none of the listed weak patterns.
The conclusion sorts take-aways by how settled they are, adds no new subtopic or body evidence, and does not end on a rephrased thesis alone.

'Paid' as a position on the calendar joins the routes, the clock and the record model, and the conclusion says why it matters (the year-end difference, the still-disputable volume). The spec's 'what the merchant controls' half is implicit only.
The author's synthesis answers the opening question with Mila's €120: finished as a forward payment on 11 March, open as a liability until at least 7 July, longer for passes.
The intro-only reader predicted all ten roadmap items in order, the three kinds of evidence and the tone; only the content of 'before and above a dispute' was a guess, and a correct one.

The answer has the cancel or reversal with no money moving and no payment appearing, then the refund as a new transaction funded from the balance that can be delayed or fail, fees not returned, and the dispute if the guest goes to the bank.
The answer has the issuer deciding under network rules with the network at arbitration, one submission before a deadline, and on a win the money withheld meanwhile, the fee and the monitoring count.

Visa rules are cited from the edition of 24 October 2026; Mastercard stages, deadlines, codes and thresholds are each attributed to Stripe or Adyen with 'not Mastercard's own text'; thresholds and fees are stated as of November 2026; Adyen's fee is set by contract with CAD 24.00 in the Canada disclosure named.
